result.title: CADMA: Capacity-Aware Coverage Decomposition for Generative Model Assessment
result.summary: Evaluating generative models requires measuring not only sample fidelity but also how well a generated set covers the real data distribution. Recent work has therefore introduced recall-oriented metrics for distribution-level evaluation. However, existing recall metrics often reduce distributional coverage to geometry-based coverage. This simplifying assumption weakens their diagnostic value and interpretability in two ways: these metrics provide only a single aggregate score that cannot distinguish essential diversity failures such as mode dropping and mode collapse, and geometry-based coverage can provide unreliable estimates by assigning high scores to poorly covered generative distributions. We therefore introduce CADMA, a capacity-aware framework for recall-oriented evaluation and diagnosis. CADMA evaluates distributional coverage through local capacity matching between real and generated samples, separating geometry-based coverage from effective coverage. This yields multi-dimensional coverage diagnostics that quantify mode dropping and mode collapse while reducing the overly optimistic estimates produced by geometry-based metrics. Through extensive experiments on toy data, real-world datasets, and generative models, we show that CADMA provides more reliable coverage estimates and more fine-grained, interpretable diagnostic signals of diversity failures than existing metrics. Our code is available at https://github.com/Open-Debin/CADMA_NeurIPS2026.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 CADMA，一种面向生成模型召回评估的容量感知框架，通过真实样本与生成样本之间的局部容量匹配，把基于几何的覆盖与有效覆盖区分开，从而对 mode dropping 与 mode collapse 给出多维诊断信号。
AI.relevance_reason: 其将覆盖度拆分为几何覆盖与有效覆盖、并区分多样性失败类型的思想，可能可供借鉴于评估并行或扩散式 latent 推理中多个 latent 假设的覆盖与坍缩，但与原论文的视觉推理场景关联较远，需核查可迁移性。
